chunks: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Yusuf Zariq al-Baghdadi narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Anbasat - a servant of Al-Rashid - quoted on the authority of Darim and Nu’aym ibn Salih al-Tabari that Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha’ (peace be upon him) quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
That God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'One of the rights of a guest is that you walk with him and escort him from the area of your house to the door.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a guest according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith traces its chain back to Imam al-Rida (a.s.), highlighting the specific etiquette of physically escorting a guest from the private interior to the threshold as a gesture of honor. This practice underscores the Islamic principle that hospitality is not merely about provision but involves active, respectful engagement, a virtue highly emphasized in Shia scholarly tradition regarding social conduct.
